linkedin_activity.text: The EU AI Act entered into force on 2 August, and one part is going to affect a lot of people quietly: Article 50(4), on labelling AI-generated content. I suspect it's about to become the next cookie banner (God forbid). Which, as we all remember, went beautifully... The official guidance is 38 pages, not everyone's taste. So I built the decision tree as a small tool: www.label-or-not.com Next time you're drafting something with AI you can run it through in about a minute. It asks a few questions and it tells you where you land, with the relevant information and a link to the official EU source on each step. Where a label is required, the tool shows the official EU icons so that you can add them to your content. Most people who generate content will be told they don't need a label, it mainly applies some professional categories and specific cases. PS: free time project, if you spot something wrong, or you have a suggestion, DM me. Free, no sign-up, no tracking.

The Super Bowl ads numbers tells a new story about the "consumer patient" Watching the ads and comparing with the last 5 years to unveil trends, comparing technology (mostly AI these days) and healthcare. The trend line is clear. While Tech spend (orange) has been somehow volatile and reaching all time highs now with AI, Pharma (in green) has entered a new era. The vertical climb (hockey stick) we see starting in 2024 isn't just about "more spending." It represents a shift in strategy: Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) engagement. The patient journey doesn't start at the clinic anymore; it starts in the living room.

linkedin_activity.text_en: Trailblazer Blog Boehringer Ingelheim : https://lnkd.in/dMBzBenq What if field service teams could access real-time decentralized knowledge anytime, anywhere – structured, searchable, and enriched with AI-powered insights? Boehringer Ingelheim has done just that with CRM Analytics and its Insight Capturing Platform INCAP: a central platform that enables more than 5,500 employees worldwide to efficiently capture and use valuable customer information. From text recognition to pharmacovigilance checks to automated feedback loops – INCAP ensures that relevant insights are not lost, but actively incorporated into decisions. Thanks to intuitive features such as voice-to-text, optical character recognition and multilingual support, INCAP can be seamlessly integrated into everyday work – without any restrictions on usability. This is how Boehringer Ingelheim creates a real single source of truth for its global knowledge. Thank you Enric for sharing your CRM Analytics success story with us – and how you can take customer centricity to the next level despite unstructured data.

meat proxy noun plural meat proxies informal, usually disparaging : a person who passes along the unexamined output of an artificial-intelligence system as their own contribution, without first understanding, verifying, interpreting, or meaningfully adapting it. Example: Rather than evaluate the reviewer’s concerns himself, he acted as a meat proxy, forwarding each comment to the coding agent and returning its response verbatim. Usage note: The term implies that the person functions merely as a human intermediary between an AI system and another person. It is especially used when the intermediary adds no judgment, expertise, accountability, or contextual understanding. 😂

Boehringer Ingelheim Reports Strong H1 2026 Sales Growth, Driven by JARDIANCE® & New Product Launches Boehringer Ingelheim delivered a strong first half of 2026, driven by robust demand for JARDIANCE®, successful U.S. launches of new medicines and continued pipeline progress across cardiometabolic disease, oncology and immunology. The company also advanced its long-term innovation strategy with positive late-stage clinical data and continued investment across both Human Pharma and Animal Health. ◾ H1 2026 Highlights • Group Net Sales: €15.8B (+16.2% CER) • Human Pharma Sales: €13.1B (+20.1% CER) • Animal Health Sales: €2.6B (+0.4% CER) • JARDIANCE® Sales: €5.7B ◾ Commercial Momentum Growth was led by continued strong demand across Human Pharma: • JARDIANCE® remained the company's largest growth driver, supported by expanding patient adoption and higher U.S. volumes. • Strong uptake of JASCAYD® (nerandomilast) for idiopathic and progressive pulmonary fibrosis following launches in the U.S., China, Japan and additional global markets. • Successful launch of HERNEXEOS® (zongertinib) for HER2-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer, marking Boehringer's return to oncology. ◾ Pipeline & Innovation Boehringer continued advancing one of the industry's broad late-stage pipelines: • Positive Phase III data for survodutide, supporting its potential in obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease. • Three new Phase III oncology studies initiated. • Continued development of obrixtamig (oncology) and apecotrep (kidney disease). • Five new compounds entered clinical development during H1. • Human Pharma pipeline now comprises approximately 80 projects. ◾ Animal Health The Animal Health business continued to strengthen its innovation portfolio: • Launch of LENZELTA®, a next-generation mastitis vaccine for dairy cattle. • Expansion of Eko Vet+™ | CANINEBEAT® AI, supporting AI-assisted detection of canine heart murmurs. • Continued support for emerging animal disease outbreaks, including New World screwworm response in the U.S. Source: https://lnkd.in/exkme8Ue Boehringer Ingelheim H1 2026 Results, Company Announcement, 15 July 2026.
